activities.title: Identifying a valid couple
activities.prompt: Which force arrangement represents a genuine couple acting on a single rigid body?

options.label: Two forces of 15 N acting in opposite directions along parallel lines separated by 0.20 m.
Two forces of 20 N and 10 N acting in opposite directions along parallel lines separated by 0.20 m.
Two forces of 15 N acting in the same direction along parallel lines separated by 0.20 m.
Two forces of 15 N acting in opposite directions directly along the same straight line of action.

feedback.A: Correct. These forces satisfy all four necessary conditions: equal magnitude (15 N), opposite direction, parallel lines of action, and separate lines of action.
feedback.B: Incorrect. The forces have unequal magnitudes (20 N and 10 N), which produces an unbalanced resultant force and translational acceleration.
feedback.C: Incorrect. The forces point in the same direction, pushing the body together rather than producing pure rotation.
feedback.D: Incorrect. The forces act along the exact same line with zero perpendicular separation, producing zero turning effect.

anchor.after: State whether the torque acts clockwise or anticlockwise.

activities.title: Calculating couple torque
activities.prompt: A couple consists of two opposite forces of magnitude 18 N acting along parallel lines separated by a perpendicular distance of 0.25 m. What is the torque produced by this couple?

feedback.A: Correct. Torque equals the product of one of the forces and the perpendicular distance: 18 N * 0.25 m = 4.5 N m.
feedback.B: Incorrect. This result doubles the force (36 N * 0.25 m). The formula requires the magnitude of one force, not both added together.
feedback.C: Incorrect. This result halves the perpendicular separation (18 N * 0.125 m). The distance in the formula is already the full separation between the lines of action.
feedback.D: Incorrect. This result multiplies both forces together with the distance (18 * 18 * 0.25). Torque uses a single force magnitude.

heading_path: Finding the perpendicular separation across different geometries
anchor.after: Then identify the side or segment that forms a 90-degree angle between them.

activities.title: Determining perpendicular separation
activities.action: Order the steps to find the torque of a couple on an irregular or angled object from first to last.
activities.prompt: Place the steps in the correct logical sequence to determine the torque of a couple from a geometric diagram.

options.label: Extend the parallel lines of action of both forces as dashed straight lines.
Identify the line segment that meets both lines of action at right angles.
Measure or calculate the shortest perpendicular distance along that 90-degree line segment.
Multiply the magnitude of one force by this perpendicular separation to calculate torque.

feedback.step_1: First step: Extend the lines of action so their paths across the geometry are clearly visible.
feedback.step_2: Second step: Locate the line segment meeting both lines of action at 90 degrees, avoiding oblique or diagonal paths.
feedback.step_3: Third step: Determine the exact length of this perpendicular line segment between the two force lines.
feedback.step_4: Fourth step: Multiply the magnitude of one force by this perpendicular distance to obtain the torque.

heading_path: Zero resultant force does not mean equilibrium
anchor.after: Therefore, zero resultant force alone does not guarantee mechanical equilibrium.

activities.title: Physical deductions for a couple
activities.prompt: A rigid body in deep space experiences only a couple consisting of two forces of magnitude 12 N separated by 0.30 m. Which statements correctly describe the body's motion and turning effect? Select all that apply.

options.label: The resultant translational force acting on the body is zero.
The body undergoes angular acceleration because the net torque is non-zero.
The torque of the couple has a value of 3.6 N m about every point in space.
The body is in complete mechanical equilibrium because the forces cancel out.

feedback.A: Correct. The forces have equal magnitude and opposite directions (12 N - 12 N = 0 N), so the resultant force is zero.
feedback.B: Correct. The torque is 12 N * 0.30 m = 3.6 N m. An unbalanced torque causes the body to experience angular acceleration.
feedback.C: Correct. The torque of a couple is independent of any pivot point and has the same value of 3.6 N m about any chosen point.
feedback.D: Incorrect. Complete mechanical equilibrium requires both zero resultant force and zero resultant torque. Here, the non-zero torque causes the object to rotate.
